title: UCAT (University Clinical Aptitude Test)
content_provenance: Subtest names, question counts and timing are reproduced from the public UCAT Consortium test format and scoring page. Weight is each subtest's share of the 184 published questions, rounded to whole percent. Skills listed are the published subtest constructs, not a verbatim objective list, and no past-paper content is transcribed.

exam.scoring: Scaled 300-900 per cognitive subtest, total 900-2700, Situational Judgement Bands 1-4

objectives.text: Identify what can be concluded from a written passage
Distinguish conclusions supported by the text from those that are not
Evaluate an argument, assumption or claim
Answer from the passage only, without outside knowledge
Draw conclusions from stated rules and conditions
Evaluate arguments and identify the strongest consideration
Interpret statistical and risk information in a scenario
Choose the most appropriate course of action under constraints
Interpret data presented in tables, charts and graphs
Perform arithmetic with percentages, ratios and rates
Work out averages, totals and cost comparisons
Identify critical factors in a situation
Judge the most and least appropriate responses
Apply professional integrity, confidentiality and safeguarding duties
Consider perspective, teamwork and the duties owed to patients and colleagues
